list_title: Building code – 2024 International Residential Code for one to three family dwellings – adopt
text_summary: Adopts the 2024 International Residential Code for one- to three-family dwellings, to take effect by Jan 1, 2027 (three-family buildings may instead use an appendix to the commercial International Building Code). Buildings with more than the small-dwelling limit are built to the commercial IBC; the 2024 code editions are exempted from several rulemaking procedure requirements.
rental_market_relevance: Sets construction standards for new one-to-three-family homes and the code path for small multifamily buildings, so it affects the cost and ease of building supply, including small rental buildings. It does not mention rentals or tenants, so the link to the rental market is indirect.

list_title: Housing – low or moderate-income – data base
text_summary: Requires the state to host an online database of low- and moderate-income rental developments (tax-credit developments at or below 60% of area median income and subsidized developments at or below 80%) with contacts, applications and special populations served. Owners of qualifying properties must list them, and new developments after Jan 1, 2027 must list at lease-up. Effective Jan 1, 2027.
rental_market_relevance: Directly about the supply and discoverability of affordable rental units. It creates a mandatory listing duty on owners and a public search tool for renters.

list_title: Landlord and tenant – victims of abuse – termination of lease
text_summary: Amends the Residential Landlord and Tenant Act to define abuse and domestic violence and to let a tenant terminate a lease early, without penalty or future rent liability, if the tenant or household member was a victim within the prior 150 days. Requires written verification, with landlord confidentiality duties.
rental_market_relevance: Directly changes tenant and landlord rights and obligations in rental agreements by creating a no-penalty exit from a lease, which affects landlord liability for lost rent.

list_title: Mortgages – prepayment penalties – limit – one to four dwelling units
text_summary: Revises limits on prepayment penalties for mortgages on real estate with up to four dwelling units: no penalty after one year, a maximum of 2% in year one, and an alternative with written disclosure and borrower consent, with no penalty after 60 months. Applies to owner-occupied homes in subsection (e). Effective on passage.
rental_market_relevance: Consumer mortgage regulation. The up-to-four-unit coverage can include small rental buildings, but the law does not mention rentals and its limits apply to owner-occupied homes.

list_title: Municipalities – emergency declarations - construction and use of SAFE Units on a temporary basis
text_summary: Defines 'SAFE Units' (small emergency shelter units of 70 to 400 sq ft with required fire, egress, electrical and ventilation features), exempts them from most of the state building code, allows municipalities to permit them temporarily under emergency declarations, and adjusts fire-code plan review timing.
rental_market_relevance: Supply-side: it creates a fast, low-cost way to add temporary emergency housing units outside the normal building code. These are shelter units, not leased rentals, so this is a borderline Rentals code.

list_title: Planning, land use, subdivision and zoning ordinances – technical amendments
text_summary: Large omnibus act that amends the Superior Court land use calendar (expedited land use appeals, briefing within 60 days of the record) and makes many technical amendments to the comprehensive planning, subdivision and zoning enabling statutes, including multi-family and accessory dwelling unit provisions, density, comprehensive permits and low- and moderate-income housing standards.
rental_market_relevance: Supply-side: the stated purpose is to cut permitting and appeal delays that block housing development. The amended statutes cover multifamily development and comprehensive permits, and the law counts multifamily rental units built under comprehensive permits toward affordable-housing goals. The page text does not show which words were added or struck, so the exact changes were not isolated.

list_title: Restrictions – guidelines – residential recovery houses
text_summary: Adds a zoning section requiring that a NARR-certified recovery residence be treated as a residential use with all residential rights, and bars local rules, including building and fire codes, from imposing restrictions beyond the Rhode Island life safety code. Effective on passage.
rental_market_relevance: Supply-side: it removes local zoning barriers to a type of group residential housing. These are supportive recovery homes rather than conventional leased rentals, so this is a borderline Rentals code.

list_title: Shoreline properties – rental disclosure – public shoreline access rights
text_summary: Amends the Residential Landlord and Tenant Act to require landlords to give tenants a written shoreline access disclosure for shoreline rentals and to notify tenants if a mortgage is 120 days delinquent. Also bars municipalities from prohibiting owners from using compliant hosting platforms for short-term rentals and requires state registration of short-term rental properties listed on hosting platforms.
rental_market_relevance: Directly about rental housing: landlord disclosure duties to tenants and the regulation of short-term rentals, which affects how much housing is available as long-term rentals.
